State the condition for limiting equilibrium: the applied horizontal force equals limiting friction, $F = \mu R$.
walkthrough:
Find the normal reaction force on the horizontal plane:
$$R = mg = 0.2(10) = 2\text{ N}$$

Equate the applied horizontal force to the limiting friction force ($F = \mu R$):
$$1.2 = \mu R$$
$$1.2 = 2\mu \implies \mu = \frac{1.2}{2} = 0.6$$

ai_rubric.Using Limiting Equilibrium: Evaluates R = 2 N and solves 1.2 = mu(2) to find mu = 0.6.

teacher_walkthrough:
Under static equilibrium on a horizontal surface, the normal reaction $R$ balances the weight of the particle:
$$R = mg = (0.2)(10) = 2\text{ N}$$

When the particle is in limiting equilibrium, the opposing friction force reaches its maximum possible value $F = \mu R$:
$$F_{\text{applied}} = \mu R$$
$$1.2 = \mu(2)$$

Divide both sides by 2 to find $\mu$:
$$\mu = \frac{1.2}{2} = 0.6$$

hints: Calculate the dynamic friction force $F = \mu R = 0.3(2) = 0.6\text{ N}$.
Apply Newton's second law: $1.2 - 0.6 = 0.2a \implies a = 3\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Note that the distance travelled in the third second is the displacement between $t = 2\text{ s}$ and $t = 3\text{ s}$.
Use $s = \frac{1}{2}at^2$ to evaluate $s(3) = 13.5\text{ m}$ and $s(2) = 6\text{ m}$, giving $\Delta s = 7.5\text{ m}$.
walkthrough:
Apply Newton's second law horizontally to find the acceleration $a$ with $\mu = 0.3$:
$$F_{\text{drive}} - \mu R = ma$$
$$1.2 - 0.3(2) = 0.2a$$
$$1.2 - 0.6 = 0.2a \implies 0.6 = 0.2a \implies a = 3\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Find the displacement from rest ($u = 0\text{ m s}^{-1}$) at $t = 2\text{ s}$ and $t = 3\text{ s}$:
$$s_3 = \frac{1}{2}a(3^2) = \frac{1}{2}(3)(9) = 13.5\text{ m}$$
$$s_2 = \frac{1}{2}a(2^2) = \frac{1}{2}(3)(4) = 6\text{ m}$$

Calculate the distance travelled in the third second:
$$\Delta s = s_3 - s_2 = 13.5 - 6 = 7.5\text{ m}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Determine the friction force when $\mu = 0.3$:
$$F = \mu R = 0.3 \times 2 = 0.6\text{ N}$$

Apply Newton's second law along the horizontal direction of motion:
$$F_{\text{net}} = ma$$
$$1.2 - 0.6 = 0.2a$$
$$0.6 = 0.2a$$

Divide both sides by 0.2 to find acceleration $a$:
$$a = \frac{0.6}{0.2} = 3\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
The phrase "distance travelled in the third second" means the distance covered from $t = 2\text{ s}$ to $t = 3\text{ s}$.
